comments.body:
## Upstream search result — the defect is real, known, and unfixed (checked 2026-10-27 ~22:10 PDT)

Searched before proposing any local fix, per the rule that "the wheel is broken" is a claim about someone else's software.

**Upstream issue: [JessicaTegner/pypandoc#447](https://github.com/JessicaTegner/pypandoc/issues/447) — "Prebuild wheel for macos pretends to be arm, while it's a intel binary"**, opened 2026-08-11 by RemiDesgrange. It reports exactly this ticket's measurement on the same version:

```
Tag: py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64
lipo -archs .venv/.../pypandoc/files/pandoc  ->  x86_64
```

and names the same reason it has become visible now: "New macOS build (since Tahoe?) will not have Rosetta include."

State of the issue as of this check: **open, no assignee, no labels, no linked branch or pull request, no milestone, and no maintainer reply in the activity log.** So there is no upstream fix to wait for and no upstream-suggested workaround to adopt.

**No newer release exists.** The PyPI simple index for `pypandoc-binary` lists macOS arm64 wheels for 1.13, 1.14, 1.15, 1.16, 1.16.2 and 1.17; **1.17 is the newest**. Upgrading cannot resolve this, and there is no post-1.17 build carrying a native binary.

### What this settles for the proposed options

- Waiting for upstream is not an option: the issue is 2.5 months old with no owner and no PR.
- Pinning a different `pypandoc_binary` version is not an option: no release ships a native arm64 pandoc.
- Option 2 (plain `pypandoc` + a host pandoc) remains viable but shifts setup onto every contributor and CI.
- **Option 1 stays the recommendation** — verify the bundled binary's architecture at bootstrap and repair it from the pinned upstream pandoc release when it does not match `uname -m`. It is portable (no CI-provider trigger), keeps the existing `pypandoc==1.17` / `pandoc 3.9` pins that `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` asserts, and self-heals every new worktree rather than requiring the manual per-venv copy.

This matches the shape already decided for the sibling host-pin bug `corking-phonolite-drafthorse` (`0461-3c72-9e38-4ce5`): fetch the required release into a version-keyed, checksum-verified cache under the repo's own cache directory, verify the download before use, and never modify what is on `PATH` or inside another tool's install. The two bugs are the same class — a pinned artifact that is not what its pin claims — and should share one bootstrap-repair mechanism rather than growing two, which also keeps the mechanism-delta ratchet satisfied.

### Still unverified

Whether the x86_64 binary is present in the Linux/Windows wheels' arm64 variants, or only in the macOS arm64 wheel. CI runs `ubuntu-latest` x86_64 and is unaffected either way, so this was not measured. No local fix was implemented in this session; the manual per-venv copy remains the only thing keeping `make verify` green on this host.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## This ticket's last acceptance criterion cannot pass, and fixing pandoc will not make it pass

"`make verify` exits 0 on an unmodified tree on arm64 macOS" is **unreachable by this ticket's work alone**. Recording it here so neither ticket gets closed on a false premise.

### Evidence

I applied this ticket's verified workaround (the native pandoc 3.9 copied over `pypandoc/files/pandoc`) in a fresh worktree branched from `ee5253abfd4`, then ran a full `make verify` — 1 h 31 m, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`:

```
22 failed, 19835 passed, 88 skipped, 48 warnings, 1 error in 5467.30s (1:31:07)
```

**The 17 reconciler failures this ticket reports are gone** — the pandoc workaround fixes exactly what it claims. What remains is a *different* cluster of 22, all in `tests/scripts/test_observability_*`, driving `infra/scripts/observability.sh`:

```
observability.sh: line 160: /var/lib/rebar/probe-region: No such file or directory
observability.sh: line 230: /var/lib/rebar/reviewbot-webhook-auth-offset: No such file or directory
subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['bash', '.../infra/scripts/observability.sh']'
  timed out after 59.99996245803777 seconds
```

`/var/lib/rebar/` does not exist on macOS and is not creatable unprivileged. That is a second, independent reason `make verify` cannot go green on this hardware, and it is unrelated to pandoc.

Filed as **`7f3d-ddc9-04d9-4861`** (`nepotistic-sensitive-arcticwolf`) and linked `relates_to` this ticket.

### Consequence for this ticket

Treat the unreachable criterion as a defect in the ticket rather than something to work around. Concretely, replace

> - [ ] `make verify` exits 0 on an unmodified tree on arm64 macOS.

with a criterion this ticket can actually satisfy and verify on its own:

> - [ ] On arm64 macOS without Rosetta, a freshly provisioned worktree resolves a pandoc whose architecture matches `uname -m`, and `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` reports 74 passed with no manual intervention.
> - [ ] `make verify` exits 0 once `7f3d-ddc9-04d9-4861` has also landed; until then the only remaining failures on this hardware are that ticket's 22 observability-script failures, and no others.

The second form is still a real gate — it forbids *any* other failure — but it does not make this ticket's closure depend on work it does not own.

### Two host facts worth carrying

Both were measured today on this host and bear on anyone verifying locally.

1. **`make verify` leaks orphaned processes.** After the run above, `ps` found **32** surviving `bash .../infra/scripts/observability.sh` processes — 16 parents, each at **PPID 1**, elapsed 8 m 19 s to 21 m 41 s. `subprocess.run(..., timeout=60)` kills only the direct child; the script's forked subshell survives and reparents to `init`. I reaped all 32 by explicit PID. Recorded in detail on `7f3d` with its own acceptance criterion, so it is findable without this conversation.
2. **Git operation cost varies by an order of magnitude here.** In the tickets tracker (213,713 index entries), a stat-only scan took 6 s while a full re-hash took 49 s. That is the root cause of bug `painted-epidermal-shelduck` and is worth knowing before reading any local timing as a code defect.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Reproduced, and the riskiest assumption tested before any code

Fresh worktree `.rebar/worktrees/bug-bb19-pypandoc` at `origin/main` = `2fb6062bfe52ffef120d5ab92038ac7227e2487c`, `.venv` on the CI-pinned Python 3.12.14, no local changes.

**Reproduction matches this ticket exactly:** the three named files report **17 failed, 57 passed**, underlying `OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`. Host facts: `platform.machine()` = `arm64`, `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` unset, no `pandoc` on `PATH`, and `/usr/bin/arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true` → "Bad CPU type in executable" (Rosetta genuinely absent).

### Architecture is readable from the file header — no `file`, no `lipo`, no exec

```
bundled .venv/.../pypandoc/files/pandoc   cffaedfe 07000001   cputype 0x01000007 = CPU_TYPE_X86_64
upstream pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc      cffaedfe 0c000001   cputype 0x0100000C = CPU_TYPE_ARM64
```

That makes the repair trigger a cheap, deterministic, Rosetta-independent static check, and it works the same way for ELF (`e_machine` at offset 18). The trigger is *architecture mismatch*, not "macOS" and not "CI" — so it is a strict no-op on every Linux and x86_64-macOS environment.

### The upstream artifact is already on the accepted-provenance list

Downloaded `https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/download/3.9/pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip` (42,595,715 bytes, zip SHA-256 `7d56ac6fe6fad0a7407bcd776aa142f61ca41838f286165f79d0584fa57b24d1`). The archive member is `pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc` — note the directory is **not** suffixed `-macOS`, unlike the zip name.

```
sha256  140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3
file    Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64
--version  pandoc 3.9
```

That digest is **already** `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256["darwin-arm64"]` at `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:69`, landed by `fda55e3655e` (ticket `9119-3f7b-22c0-4421`). So the binary the bootstrap will fetch is the one the repo's provenance check already sanctions, and the plan asserts that membership in a test so the two cannot drift apart.

### Why CI is green while this host is red

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:755` sets `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS` to `platform_compat and not external` on `macos-latest`. The 17 reconciler tests are not `platform_compat`, so the macOS cell never runs them; the Ubuntu cells run them against a correct x86_64 Linux wheel. CI therefore cannot see this defect and will not see the fix either — which is why the plan's trigger has to be architecture rather than a CI step. CI also runs `pytest` directly (`_build-and-test.yml:763`), never `make install`, so the bootstrap repair never executes on a runner.

### Where the fix goes, and why not the two obvious places

Replacing `.venv/.../pypandoc/files/pandoc` in place (this ticket's manual workaround) is rejected: `uv sync` restores the broken binary and it falsifies the wheel's recorded hashes. Putting the native binary on `PATH` is also rejected: `docs/local-dev-env.md:35-66` records that pypandoc probes every candidate and keeps the **highest** executable version, so a Homebrew pandoc 3.11 would beat a 3.9 in `.venv/bin` and break the `pandoc 3.9` pin assertion. `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` is the only reliable override, and `.tools/bin` is the repo's existing home for pinned, digest-verified third-party binaries (`Makefile:51`, `Makefile:467-482` for `actionlint`).

The plan is now written into the description, with file impact declared. Running `review-plan` next.

comments.body:
Implementation landed in the worktree `bug-bb19-pypandoc` (branch at `2fb6062bfe5`). Plan review PASSED and signed at that SHA; ticket claimed.

What was built, and what each piece is evidenced by:

- `scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` — reads the first 20 bytes of the pypandoc-bundled pandoc and decodes the architecture from the Mach-O or ELF header. Match → exit 0, no network. Mismatch with a repo-local native binary already present → reuse it, no network. Mismatch with nothing to reuse → download the pinned upstream release, verify the **extracted** binary's SHA-256, install to `.tools/bin/pandoc` with mode 0755. Mismatch with no pin for the host → `PandocRepairError`, loud, with the manual recipe.
- `Makefile` — `ensure-pandoc` target (doc-commented, `.PHONY`), invoked by `install` between `uv sync` and `hooks`. The recipe prefers `.venv/bin/python` when it exists: `make install` is often run unactivated, and an ambient interpreter that cannot import pypandoc would turn the repair into a silent no-op, which is the defect class this ticket exists to remove.
- `tests/conftest.py` — `_select_repo_pandoc()`, called from `pytest_configure`. An explicit `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` always wins; the absent case costs one `is_file()` and imports nothing, so CI does no work.
- `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` — 17 tests, download boundary injected, no sockets.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`, `NOTICE` — automatic path documented; the manual recipe demoted to the offline fallback; the developer-only fetch recorded against the GPL obligation.

Measured outcomes:

- `make ensure-pandoc` → installed `.tools/bin/pandoc`, 189,626,864 bytes. `file` reports `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64`; `--version` reports `pandoc 3.9`.
- With **no** `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` exported and no manual step: the 3 reconciler modules report **74 passed in 5.10s** (17 failed / 57 passed before the change).
- With `.tools/bin/pandoc` moved aside: `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` **FAILS** (`OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`) rather than skipping, so the pin keeps its teeth.
- `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` → 17 passed.
- `make lint` rc=0; `make typecheck` rc=0 (750 files); `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` rc=0 (`new=26`, all pre-existing and marker-admitted, none mine); `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` rc=0 (`new=0 increased=0`).

One defect found and fixed during implementation rather than in review: loading `scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` from the root conftest by file location crashed the whole session with `INTERNALERROR ... AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'`. `@dataclass` resolves its owning module out of `sys.modules`, and `module_from_spec` does not register it. The module is now registered before `exec_module`. It only reproduced once `.tools/bin/pandoc` existed, which is why the first test run was green.

`make verify` is running now.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

On arm64 macOS without Rosetta, 17 reconciler tests fail on a clean tree: `pypandoc_binary` 1.17's `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel bundles an **x86_64** pandoc. uv picked the right wheel; its contents are wrong. Upstream [pypandoc#447](https://github.com/JessicaTegner/pypandoc/issues/447) is open, unassigned, no PR, and 1.17 is the newest release.

Reproduced at `2fb6062bfe5`, no local changes: `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` → **17 failed, 57 passed**, `OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`.

Two commits already landed for this defect class. `9af50584d0a` documents a **manual** download plus `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` export (`docs/local-dev-env.md:35-66`); `fda55e3655e` widened provenance to accept the native arm64 binary (`scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:65-72`). The remaining gap is making it **automatic**, so a fresh worktree is not born red.

## Approach

Repair at **bootstrap**, triggered by an **architecture mismatch** rather than a platform name or a CI provider.

`scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` reads the first 16 bytes of the pandoc `pypandoc` bundles, decoding the architecture from the Mach-O or ELF header. Measured here: the bundled binary's header is `cffaedfe 07000001` (cputype `0x01000007` = `CPU_TYPE_X86_64`) while `platform.machine()` is `arm64`. When the decoded architecture matches the host the script exits 0 having touched no network — that is every Linux and x86_64-macOS environment, including all CI cells. On a mismatch it downloads the pinned upstream release, verifies the **extracted binary's** SHA-256 against a hard-coded pin, then installs it to the git-ignored `.tools/bin/pandoc`.

That shape is already in the repo: `Makefile:467-482` (`actionlint-bin`) installs a pinned, SHA-256-verified third-party binary into `.tools/bin` (`Makefile:51`). Reusing it adds no new mechanism kind, keeps the download out of `.venv` (where `uv sync` would overwrite it, falsifying the wheel's recorded hashes), never touching `PATH`.

Selection must use `PYPANDOC_PANDOC`, not `PATH`: pypandoc probes every candidate, keeping the **highest** version it can execute, so a Homebrew pandoc 3.11 would beat a 3.9 in `.venv/bin`, breaking the `pandoc 3.9` pin assertion (`docs/local-dev-env.md:35-66` records this). So `tests/conftest.py` sets `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` to `.tools/bin/pandoc` when that file exists, the variable is unset, the file's decoded architecture matches the host. When the file is absent the hook does nothing — no import, no work beyond one `exists()` — so CI behaviour is unchanged.

Two assumptions were tested before writing code. First, `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` alone is sufficient: exporting it in this worktree turns the command above into **74 passed** with the broken wheel binary left in place. Second, the upstream artifact is the one the repo already accepts: the member `pandoc-3.9-arm64/bin/pandoc` of `pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip` hashes to `140353e19f2518a76aa144ce90a7afcb6f485ba94d0dbe069e77c805277908c3`, which is already `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256["darwin-arm64"]` at `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:69`. A test asserts that membership so the fetched artifact cannot drift from the provenance allowlist.

On a mismatch the script cannot repair, `make install` **fails loudly** with the manual recipe in its message. Silent degradation is the defect this ticket exists to remove.

## Scope

- `scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` — new. Mach-O/ELF architecture decoding, the pinned download table, digest-verified install into `.tools/bin`, plus `repo_pandoc_for_host()` for the test-time lookup.
- `Makefile` — new `ensure-pandoc` target modelled on `actionlint-bin`; `install` invokes it after `uv sync`.
- `tests/conftest.py` — set `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` from `.tools/bin/pandoc` when present, arch-matched. `_REPO_ROOT` already exists at line 115.
- `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` — new regression tests. `tests/scripts/conftest.py:26-28` already puts `scripts/` on `sys.path`, so the module imports by bare name.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — document the automatic path; keep the manual steps as the offline fallback.
- `NOTICE` — record that the dev bootstrap may fetch the same pandoc 3.9 from `jgm/pandoc` releases into a git-ignored directory. Nothing is vendored or redistributed.

## Testing

In `tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py` (marker `scripts`), with the network boundary injected — no test downloads anything:

- **No-op branch:** synthetic Mach-O arm64 header on an `arm64` host. `ensure()` reports "matches", never calling the injected downloader, which raises if called.
- **Repair branch:** mismatched bundled binary plus an injected downloader returning bytes matching the pin. `ensure()` writes `.tools/bin/pandoc`, making it executable.
- **Failure path:** the injected downloader returns bytes whose digest does not match the pin. `ensure()` raises; `.tools/bin/pandoc` does not exist afterwards. A silently-accepted bad download would reintroduce an unrunnable binary.
- **Edge paths:** `read_binary_arch` decodes Mach-O `cffaedfe 07000001` → `x86_64`, Mach-O `cffaedfe 0c000001` → `arm64`, ELF `e_machine` `0x3e` → `x86_64`, ELF `0xb7` → `arm64`, returning `None` for a short or unknown file, so an unrecognised format degrades to "no mismatch", never to a spurious download.
- **Absent/mismatched path:** `repo_pandoc_for_host()` returns `None` when `.tools/bin/pandoc` is absent, also when it is present but its decoded architecture differs from the host.
- **Pin-drift guard:** the digest `ensure_pandoc.py` pins is a member of `ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256["darwin-arm64"]`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After `make install` on this arm64 macOS host, `file .tools/bin/pandoc` reports `Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64`.
- [x] `.tools/bin/pandoc --version | head -1` reports `pandoc 3.9`.
- [x] With no `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` exported, `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` reports **74 passed** (it reports 17 failed, 57 passed today).
- [x] With `.tools/bin/pandoc` deleted, `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` FAILS rather than skips; checked by reading that node's outcome.
- [x] `python scripts/ensure_pandoc.py` exits 0 when the decoded architecture matches the host; checked by the no-op-branch test.
- [x] That same no-op run performs no network access; checked by the injected downloader, which raises if called.
- [x] `tests/conftest.py` sets no environment variable when `.tools/bin/pandoc` is absent; checked by the `repo_pandoc_for_host()` absent-path test.
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/test_ensure_pandoc.py -q` reports all tests passing, including the bad-digest case.
- [x] `make verify` from this worktree shows zero failures in `tests/unit/reconciler/`. The only remaining failures on this hardware are the 22 `tests/scripts/test_observability_*` failures owned by `7f3d-ddc9-04d9-4861`. (The original "`make verify` exits 0" criterion is unreachable by this ticket alone — see the comment of 2026-10-27.)
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0.

file_impact.reason: New: decode the bundled pandoc's Mach-O/ELF architecture, and on mismatch install the pinned, digest-verified upstream pandoc 3.9 into the git-ignored .tools/bin; also exposes repo_pandoc_for_host() for the test-time lookup.
New ensure-pandoc target modelled on the existing actionlint-bin pinned-binary install; make install invokes it after uv sync.
Point PYPANDOC_PANDOC at .tools/bin/pandoc when it exists, is arch-matched, and the user has not set the variable; strict no-op otherwise.
New regression coverage: arch decoding for Mach-O and ELF, the no-op branch, the repair branch, the bad-digest refusal, and the pin-vs-accepted-digest drift guard.
Replace the manual-only arm64 pandoc prerequisite with the automatic bootstrap path, keeping the manual steps as the offline fallback.
Record that the dev bootstrap may fetch the same pandoc 3.9 from jgm/pandoc releases into a git-ignored directory; nothing becomes vendored or redistributed.
